artifacts.summary: Four-phase plan closing the five durability gaps in the already-working tagged Sapience write path: stale domain-doc corrections plus the four-population census, an explicit disposition for all four MCP write tools, the SessionStart-nudge redirect in EXTENSION.md, write-side dry-run test coverage asserting [repo:<slug>], and a registered advisory write-path rule landed with the redeploy.

user_decision.question: settings-fragment.json still grants all four MCP write tools at this repo's project scope, including two the extension's own text says never to use. Keeping the grant leaves a stray proactive MCP call able to succeed non-interactively and land a permanent, undeletable untagged write; narrowing it adds a mechanical second line of defense but leaves core/context/patterns/mcp-server-ownership.md's worked example (which cites the current four-tool grant by path) stale, and core/ is outside this task's declared edit target.
options: Keep the four-tool grant intact; record the residual and its promotion criterion in the new write-path rule (this plan's route)
Narrow the grant now by dropping sapience_remember and sapience_wrapup from the allow-list, accepting that mcp-server-ownership.md's worked example goes stale until a follow-up task fixes it
Keep the grant here and file a separate follow-up task that narrows it together with the core/ worked-example update, so neither surface is left inconsistent
user_decision.recommended: Keep the four-tool grant intact; record the residual and its promotion criterion in the new write-path rule (this plan's route)
user_decision.obligation: Deliverable (b) and acceptance criterion 3: the standing rule must exist with its advisory-or-enforced status recorded. The recommended route discharges this with an advisory, path-scoped rules/sapience-write-path.md whose own text records the kept-grant residual, the rejected-mechanization rationale, and the promotion criterion that would justify enforcement -- checkable by reading that file after Phase 4.

memory_candidates.content: Extension-authoring plans in this codebase must be decomposed around two check-extension-docs.sh rules that force same-phase atomicity, neither of which is obvious from the plan standards alone. Rule H (check_undeclared_rules) FAILS on a rules/*.md file present on disk but absent from its extension manifest's provides.rules, so creating a rule file and registering it can never be two separate green commits -- the pair is one atomic-batch objective. Rule R (check_line_count_accuracy) FAILS on a stale line_count in an extension's source index-entries.json, so any phase editing an indexed context/** file must repair index-entries.json in that same phase (bash .claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write) rather than deferring it to the deploy phase, or that phase's own --only-gate 3 check fails. Separately, Rule U caps EXTENSION.md at 60 lines, which is a real ceiling for any plan adding prose there. Also: an extension script that sources ${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/common.sh cannot run from the source store at all (lib/ exists only in the post-deploy flattened .claude/scripts/ tree), so its tests must build a deployed-layout scratch fixture.
